title: Protocol for cross-platform characterization of human and murine extracellular vesicles and particles
protocol: Dilute EVP samples in PBS in a 2 mL Eppendorf tube.
Set focus: Dilute standard 100 nm beads 1:500 in PBS.
Store diluted beads at 4°C for up to one month.
Click on LOAD.
Click on CAPTURE.
Click on START CAMERA.
Move the stage to the ideal laser beam position with even distribution of particles.
Focus on the beads by moving to the ideal imaging plane.
Adjust the CAMERA LEVEL until the maximum number of EVPs can be seen.
Transfer the loading tube to the waste.
Remove the tube containing the beads.
Click on FLUSH.
Place the sample in the tube holder.
Introduce the loading tubing into the sample, ensuring it is fully submerged.
Click on LOAD.
Click on CAPTURE.
Focus on the particles.
Set SCREEN GAIN to 1.
Ensure CAMERA LEVEL does not exceed 12.
Create an experiment folder and type in the file name.
Select the acquisition script.
Set RECORDDILUTION to 3000.
Set SETVISCOSITY to WATER.
Display CAMERASETTINGSMSG.
Perform SYRINGELOAD of 1000.
Delay for 20 seconds.
Perform SYRINGELOAD of 100.
Delay for 10 seconds.
Start REPEATSTART.
Capture for 60 seconds.
Delay for 1 second.
Repeat the process twice more.
Stop SYRINJECT.
Process SINGLESETTING.
Export RESULTS.
Run script for NS500 analysis.
Go to ANALYSIS and open the experiment file.
Process selected files and export results as PDF files.
Click on FLUSH to flush out the remaining sample.
Disconnect the tube from the PBS bottle and click on EMPTY FLUIDICS.
Plug in the Milli-Q water bottle to the tubing.
Click on PRIME FLUIDICS and wait until fluidics is primed.
Disconnect the tubing from the bottle and click on EMPTY FLUIDICS.
Switch off NS500 and the computer after acquisition is done.
Dilute EVP samples in PBS to a final concentration of 0.1 μg/μL of EVP protein.
Place the required number of coated grids into the chamber of a plasma cleaner.
Run the cycle to neutralize any static charges on the grids.
Place 5 μL of sample on a formvar/carbon-coated 400 mesh copper grid.
Allow the sample to settle for 1 minute.
Dry the sample by touching the edge of the grid with a wedge of Whatman Grade 1 filter paper and wicking away the solution.
Negatively stain with 4 successive drops of 1.5% aqueous solution of uranyl acetate (UrAc).
Dry between each drop by wicking the solution away from the grid.
Air-dry the grid.
Mount prepared grid in sample holder.
Insert sample holder into the TEM column and wait for the vacuum to equilibrate.
Turn on the filament.
Image the grids with JEOL JEM 1400 transmission electron microscope operating at 100 kV.
Capture images on a Veleta 2 K × 2 K CCD camera.
Capture 10–15 images from each of 3 randomly selected areas of each grid at 50,000x and 100,000x lens magnification.
Take a volume corresponding to 5 μg of EVP in PBS.
Place the sample in a low-protein binding Eppendorf tube.
Dry the samples using a vacuum centrifuge at 200 mTorr until dryness is achieved.
If necessary, freeze the sample vials in liquid nitrogen and repeat vacuum centrifugation.
Dissolve, denature, and reduce proteins in the EVP sample.
Add 25 μL denaturing buffer to the dried EVP samples.
Incubate at room temperature (20°C–22°C) for 1 hour under vigorous shaking.
Prepare a 100 mM iodoacetamide (IAA) solution by dissolving 18.5 mg IAA in 1 mL 50 mM ABC.
Add 5 μL IAA solution to each EVP sample.
Incubate at room temperature (20°C–22°C), in the dark, for 1 hour with vigorous shaking.
Lower the urea concentration by adding 30 μL of 50 mM ABC to each sample.
Dissolve Endopeptidase Lys-C stock in 180 μL of 50 mM ABC to obtain a concentration of 0.1 μg/μL.
Add 5 μL Lys-C solution to each tube.
Incubate on a shaker at room temperature (20°C–22°C) overnight.
Lower the urea concentration further by adding 65 μL of 50 mM ABC to each sample.
Dissolve aliquoted lyophilized trypsin in 200 μL of 50 mM ABC.
Add 5 μL of trypsin solution to each sample.
Incubate on shaker at room temperature (20°C–22°C) for 6 hours.
Halt digestion by adding 1 μL neat trifluoroacetic acid (TFA).
Place pre-labeled micro-purification tips in a compatible table-top centrifuge.
If a centrifuge does not fit pipette tips, make a hole in the lid of a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube, place the tip inside, and insert the tube into the centrifuge.
Push the tip further into the tube if necessary to ensure the centrifuge can close properly.
Place the micro-purification tip in the centrifuge and add 70 μL of activation solvent to the tip.
Centrifuge until the activation solvent passes through but avoid dehydration of the column material.
Place 70 μL of Equilibration/washing solvent in each tube.
Centrifuge until the liquid has been pushed through.
Repeat step with Equilibration/washing solvent, placing a small drop (approx. 10 μL) and spinning for 1–2 s.
Place the samples in the correct pre-labeled tips.
Centrifuge until all liquid has been pushed through.
Wash the tips by placing 70 μL of Equilibration/washing solvent in each tip.
Continue to centrifuge until the liquid has been pushed through.
Elute the peptides by connecting the modified combi-tip to the micro-purification tip.
Push 70 μL of Elution solvent through the tip.
Place samples in vacuum centrifuge at room temperature until completely dry.
Dissolve dried peptides by adding 8 μL of 0.1% TFA to each HPLC vial and vortexing for 5 seconds.
Ensure liquid is located at the bottom of the tube after dissolving.
Inject 3 μL from each dissolved sample into the mass spectrometer.
Program the mass spectrometer using a linear gradient from 1% B/99% A to 35% B/65% A over 90 minutes.
Query and analyze tandem MS data using proteomic databases and statistical software.
Process high resolution/high mass accuracy nano-LC-MS/MS data using Proteome Discoverer 1.4.1.14/Mascot 2.5 software.
Calculate the relative abundance of a given protein from the average area of the three most intense peptide signals.
Assign an area of zero to proteins with area intensities below the minimum range or undetected proteins.
Query human data against the UniProt’s Complete HUMAN proteome.
Query mouse data against UniProt’s Complete MOUSE proteome.
Use Trypsin/P with a maximum of 2 missed cleavage sites.
Set monoisotopic precursor mass tolerance to 10 ppm.
Set monoisotropic fragment mass tolerance to 0.02 Da.
Include dynamic modifications: Oxidation (M), Acetyl (Protein N-term).
Include static modification: Carbamidomethyl (C).
Apply Percolator to calculate peptide False Discovery Rates (FDR) per file with an FDR of 1% for each LC-MS/MS file.
For EVP-enriched samples in contact with Fetal Bovine Serum (FBS), concatenate a bovine-specific database to human and mouse databases.
For plasma and tissue samples, concatenate sequences of porcine trypsin and Endopeptidase Lys-C to human and mouse databases for exclusion.
Collapse probe values at the protein level using the probe with maximum intensity when multiple UniProt IDs are identified for proteins.
Apply Log2 transformation to proteomic expression data.
Consider quantile normalization if changes across samples are due to unwanted technical variability.
Import proteomic expression data into R program.
Normalize between arrays using ‘normalizeBetweenArrays’ function (method = quantile) from the Limma package.
Visualize proteomic data.
Use heatmaps and clustering for data visualization.
Generate a heatmap using the GENE-E software.
Conduct principal component analysis (PCA) using the ‘princomp()’ function with default options using the R program.
Illustrate PCA results in a three-dimensional plot using the ‘rgl’ package and ‘plot3d()’ function.
Apply the t-SNE algorithm to generate t-SNE plots using the ‘Rtsne’ R package.
Conduct consensus clustering to assess whether proteomic expression differs between sample groups using the GENE-E software.
Perform biomarker selection using GENE-E software.
Sort proteins by signal-to-noise statistic.
Calculate the signal-to-noise ratio as (μA - μB)/(αA + αB).
Where μ and α represent the mean and standard deviation of proteomic expression, respectively, for each class.
Use the signal to noise marker selection tool from GENE-E with 1,000 permutations.
Apply a fold change cut-off of ≥10 and FDR <0.05 to select tumor-specific markers.
Set criteria for marker selection including mean protein expression ≥108 with positivity in ≥80% of the corresponding sample type.
Apply the Random Forest algorithm to identify biomarkers differentiating sample groups.
Use Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) provided by the caret R package with ten-fold cross-validation for feature selection.
Determine the minimal number of top proteins based on variable importance measure accuracy.
Conduct Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) to identify significant biological functions or pathways related to identified proteins.
Use tweezers to handle chips carefully.
Avoid touching the center square of the chip to prevent damage to antibodies on the surface.
Fill the space between wells in a 24-well plate with dH2O to prevent samples from drying.
Place pre-scanned chips in inner wells of the 24-well plate, leaving some space between the corners of the chip and the well wall.
Carefully load 35 μL of diluted sample onto the central square of the chip.
Avoid touching the chip surface with the pipette tip to prevent damage.
Check that the sample is retained on the chip by surface tension.
Incubate overnight (16 h) at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Place a lid and aluminum foil on the plate to protect samples from light.
Avoid contact or movement until the next step.
Add 1000 μL of solution A to each well containing a chip.
Place the 24-well plate on an orbital shaker and shake at 500 RPM for 3 min at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Remove 750 μL of solution A from the well.
Add 750 μL of fresh solution A to each well carefully without touching the chip surface with the pipette tip.
Shake the 24-well plate at 500 RPM for 3 min at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Repeat steps involving washing and antibody addition two more times for a total of 3 washes.
After the last wash, remove 750 μL of solution A from each well.
Add 250 μL of antibody mixture to each well.
Gently pipette solution to mix thoroughly.
Place a lid on the 24-well plate and wrap in aluminum foil.
Incubate the plate for 1 hour at room temperature (20°C–22°C) without shaking.
Add 500 μL of solution A to each well.
Remove 750 μL of solution A immediately after addition.
Add 750 μL of fresh solution A to each well.
Shake the plate at 500 RPM for 3 minutes at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Remove 750 μL of solution A from each well.
Add 750 μL of solution B to each well.
Shake the plate at 500 RPM for 3 minutes at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Repeat steps involving solutions A and B two more times, for a total of three repetitions.
Remove 750 μL from each well after the final shaking with solution B.
Add 750 μL of Milli-Q water to each well.
Shake the plate at 500 RPM for 3 minutes at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Fill three 60 cm cell culture dishes with Milli-Q water.
Transfer one chip from the well using flat tip tweezers by pushing it against the wall and lifting up from one side.
Hold the sides of the chip carefully without touching the surface to transfer it.
Place the chip horizontally in deionized water in a cell culture dish and shake gently with tweezers several times.
Do not allow the chip surface to dry during washing steps.
Coat the chip surface with water when moving from one wash to another.
Ensure the chips are always facing up during washing steps.
Repeat steps for a second 6-cm dish as previously described.
Repeat steps for a third 6-cm dish as previously described.
Dry the chip by lifting at a 45° angle from Milli-Q water.
Place the dried chip on paper, facing up, until completely dry.
Initiate ExoScan 2.5.5 acquisition software.
Plug the USB supplied with the ExoView kit into the computer.
Choose the corresponding chip ID number for the chip to be scanned.
Place the chip on the stage and start scanning.
Initiate ExoViewer 2.5.0 software.
Set sizing threshold to 50-200 nm diameter.
Acquire the chip.
Go over each spot to confirm they were not damaged during previous steps.
Choose spots for analysis by the software.
Transfer the necessary amount of EVPs into new Eppendorf tubes and keep them on ice.
Add an equal volume of Lysis buffer to all EVP samples run on the same gel.
Mix well.
Place the Eppendorf tube on an orbital shaker.
Incubate for 30 min at 4°C.
Measure protein concentration using BCA assay in a microplate according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Transfer 5 μg of cell line or tissue-derived EVP protein extracts into new 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes and keep them on ice.
Transfer 20 μg of plasma-derived EVP protein extracts into new 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes and keep them on ice.
Add loading buffer stock solution to EVP samples to achieve a final concentration of 1X.
Place the samples in a heat block at 100°C for 5 minutes.
Spin down the samples for 1 minute at 12,000 × g at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Load the supernatant into the wells of the commercial polyacrylamide gel.
Place a gradient Tris-glycine gel in the electrophoresis tank.
Add running buffer up to the top of the gel.
Rinse the wells with running buffer using a clean loading tip or syringe.
Load the samples and ladder into the wells.
Run gel for 30 min at 100 V.
Continue running gel for 60 min at 150 V.
Prepare PVDF membrane and transfer buffer while gel is running.
Place transfer buffer in refrigerator for at least 1 h before use.
Activate PVDF membrane with methanol for 10 seconds.
Rinse activated PVDF membrane several times with transfer buffer.
Rock PVDF membrane gently on a shaker at room temperature for 2–3 minutes.
Soak sponges and filter paper rectangles in cold transfer buffer.
Cut off wells and bottom of gel to make it flat.
Assemble transfer sandwich from the bottom up as depicted.
Remove bubbles between gel and PVDF membrane with pipette or tube.
Fill gel transfer tank with fresh transfer buffer from the top.
Insert assembled transfer sandwich into gel transfer tank.
Run 1 hour at 100 V at 4°C in the cold room or in a bucket filled with ice.
Turn off the power source after transfer completion.
Carefully unpack the sandwich and place the PVDF membrane, protein side up, in a box containing blocking buffer to cover it completely.
Place the box on a rocker at room temperature (20°C–22°C) or in the cold room (4°C) for at least 1 hour.
Pour off the blocking buffer after incubation.
Add 5–10 mL of primary antibody diluted in blocking buffer to the appropriate concentration to the membrane-containing box.
Incubate overnight on a rocking platform in the cold room (4°C).
Pour off the primary antibody.
Wash three times, 10 min each, with washing buffer on a rocking platform in the cold room (4°C).
Add 5–10 mL HRP-conjugated secondary antibody diluted 1:10000 in washing buffer to the appropriate concentration.
Incubate at room temperature (20°C–22°C) or in the cold room (4°C), with rocking, for 1–1.5 h.
Pour off the secondary antibody.
Wash three times, 10 min each, with washing buffer on a rocking platform at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
During the last wash, prepare the ECL reagent by mixing equal volumes of each component of HRP substrate (ECL reagent A and B).
Pour off the washing buffer.
Add the ECL mix to the membrane.
Incubate for 1 min.
Remove the ECL mix and transfer the membrane to an autoradiography cassette or a ChemiDoc station.
Develop the autoradiography film in the dark room, determining the optimal exposure time empirically (5 s - 5 min).
Isolate extracellular vesicles via ultracentrifugation.
Measure total protein content of isolated vesicles by BCA assay as per manufacturer’s instructions.
Dilute EVP samples at a concentration of 10–30 μg/mL in coating buffer.
For EVP samples with a concentration higher than 50 μg/mL, dilute in 1x coating buffer to obtain a 10–30 μg/mL suspension.
For EVP samples with a concentration lower than 50 μg/mL, including unfractionated plasma and culture supernatant, dilute at a 1:1 ratio with 2x coating buffer to obtain a 10–30 μg/mL suspension.
Empirically determine the ideal EVP concentration for immobilization by preparing serial dilutions of the EVP suspension.
Analyze the final signal-to-noise ratio to select the optimal EVP concentration.
Pipette 50 μL of the EVP suspension into the wells of a 96-well plate.
Ensure the solution covers the bottom of each well completely.
Repeat pipetting for each sample in triplicate, including two wells for protein-specific antibodies and at least one well for isotype controls.
Incubate the plate overnight (12–20 h) at 4°C, in the dark without shaking.
Remove unbound EVPs by washing 3 times in PBS.
Carefully aspirate all supernatant from each well.
Slowly pipette 100 μL of sterile PBS per well using a multichannel pipettor.
Incubate 5 min at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Carefully aspirate the PBS.
Repeat steps to wash with PBS two times for a total of 3 washes.
Passively adsorb EVPs onto microwells via an alkaline bicarbonate coating buffer.
Form hydrophobic interactions between EVP proteins and plastic for immobilization.
Label the EVP membrane with a lipophilic dye according to manufacturer’s instructions before immobilization.
Acquire fluorescent signals after the first wash using a plate reader or microscope.
Perform aspiration and pipetting steps with extreme care, ensuring not to scratch the surface of the well.
Equilibrate the pipet tip with reagent before loading.
Pipette buffers slowly onto the wall of the well, allowing liquid to flow to the bottom of the well.
Aspirate PBS from each well.
Pipette 100 μl of 0.2% Triton-X in TBS into each well.
Incubate for 5 min at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Wash the wells two times with PBS (2 × 5 min incubation at room temperature (20°C–22°C)).
Aspirate PBS from each well.
Pipette 100 μl of TNB blocking buffer in each well.
Incubate for 1 hour at room temperature (20°C–22°C) in the dark.
Aspirate TNB buffer from each well.
Pipette 30 μL of the primary antibody/isotype control solution into each well without washing the plate.
Incubate the plate overnight (12–20 hours) at 4°C in the dark.
Wash the plate 3 times with PBS (5 minutes per wash at room temperature).
Pipette 30 μL of the secondary antibody solution into each well.
Incubate the plate for 2 hours at room temperature (20°C–22°C) in the dark.
Aspirate the secondary antibody solution.
Wash the plate 3 times with PBS (5 minutes per wash at room temperature).
Aspirate the PBS from each well.
Pipette 200 μL of PBS into each well.
Acquire the plate using a plate reader equipped with fluorescence module or a fluorescence imaging system (e.g., Odyssey, Licor).
Set acquisition parameters as follows: bottom reading; integration time = 1 s; PMT sensitivity = Auto.
